hypothesis: gfx1201 MXFP8 is more faithful because it uses make_wave_block32 (block-hoisted E8M0 scale) and native v_cvt_f32_fp8, while gfx1030 MXFP8 reloads the scale per element via BlockCodec::load.
method: Diagnostic build only: the gfx1201 wave-block branch inside sllm_matmul_mxfp8_w8a8_m1_col2_body was enabled for gfx1030 as well. Same forced prefix, same BF16 baseline, same device.

control_bf16.interpretation: the diagnostic build does not touch the BF16 path

verdict: HYPOTHESIS REJECTED. The two decode paths produce bit-identical logits on gfx1030.
why: decode_scaled(value, scale) fuses the E8M0 exponent add into the FP32 bit pattern; load_wave_block32 computes decode(value) * decode(scale). For a power-of-two scale both are exact in the normal range. The lane-to-K assignment is also identical (thread wave*32+lane covers elements wave*32+lane+256j in both), so the FP32 accumulation order is unchanged. Only the mechanism for reading the scale byte differs, and that carries the same value.
remaining_candidates: the gfx1201 BF16 baseline itself differs (the two GPUs disagree on 4.8% of positions), so within-GPU agreement rates are measured against different references and are not directly comparable across GPUs
other MXFP8-path kernels on gfx1201 (activation quantizer, attention route) rather than the M=1 matmul decode
MXFP6 near-tie flip rate is stable across GPUs (0.386 gfx1030 / 0.405 gfx1201) while MXFP8 varies (0.420 / 0.238); the MXFP8-specific variation is unexplained by the matmul decode
